grh_7ad535977a6379531000.title: The Girl with the Gazelle
paragraphs: Sir Henry Davenant fears Moriarty has replaced his priceless Girl with a Gazelle inside an impregnable time-locked strong room, and Holmes's own paint test seems to confirm that the picture is a modern copy. The impossible theft is the clue. Holmes discovers that trusted employee Jackson is linked to Moriarty and realizes the painting was never stolen at all. The supposed expert Delac, his disappearance and the bloodstains were staged to draw Holmes in, while Violet had prepared a small area of the genuine painting so Holmes's test would falsely condemn it as modern. Moriarty's aim was to make Davenant willingly hand the real painting to Violet for removal. Jackson escapes after locking the investigators in the strong room, but the original remains safe.

The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.bbd501bf461d302b|Petri Wines]] and [[org|org.bbd501bf461d302b|Petri Wines]].
This version is based on [[work|work.doyle.8ed51516212d2ff8|The Final Problem]]. Arthur Conan Doyle is credited as author.

grh_7aa27bb6409fb2a55013.title: The Emperor of San Francisco
paragraphs: After losing his fortune in San Francisco, Joshua Norton responds by proclaiming himself Emperor of the United States and gradually becomes a tolerated, generous local institution. He befriends an opera singer calling herself Countess Esther, helps soften the arrogant manager Peter Briggs and watches the pair marry. Years later, as Norton lies dying, he begins to doubt whether his imperial life was only a delusion. Esther admits that her own title was invented too but insists that his kindness made him a true emperor in the way that mattered, and she sings for him at his final request.
